findings.evidence: GN6 says codes-cli.test.ts runs the tool as the script runs it. It specifies two staging cases: no key-check row gives CODES_KEY_CHECK_ABSENT with no batch row or directory, and a row stored under another pepper gives CODES_PEPPER_MISMATCH. Both use 'generated peppers, since a test-only value is refused outside APP_ENV=test'. GN1 has loadCodeToolConfig read MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL 'with the app's rules'. But in every CI job the owner URL carries the password ci_test-only_owner (.github/workflows/ci.yml lines 42, 75, 87, 107; tools/env-init.ts lines 190-202 require the CI owner password to contain test-only). src/lib/server/config/index.ts lines 279-284 refuse every key whose raw value contains test-only unless APP_ENV is test. A generator spawned under APP_ENV=staging in CI therefore fails with ConfigError test_only on MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL before it connects. It never reaches the require-mode key check, so the only tests of INV10's staging half fail in CI. They pass locally, where the development profile generates the owner password. This breaks the plan's own contract that each refusal is reached with inputs every earlier check accepts. It also invites the wrong fix: relaxing the Phase 1 test-only rule for tools.
findings.fix: Say how these cases run in CI without weakening the config rule. For example, call createBatch() and ensureCodeKey() in-process, with the environment passed as an explicit parameter or a parsed config object built by the test, and assert the tags there. Keep spawned runs only for refusals that come before any connection, and say that those (GN2's confirmations) happen before a database connection. State that the test-only rule is not changed, and add a source check that loadCodeToolConfig applies it.

findings.evidence: INV7 says product-agnostic.test.ts proves that 'every product literal in tools/ and tests/ comes from tools/codes/demo.ts ... or is one of the synthetic test prefixes AAA, QRS and ZZZ'. The snapshot already has ARM product literals in tests: tests/blackbox/log-privacy.test.ts lines 22, 25 and 26 (ARM-${crockford(4)}-...) and tests/unit/log-schema.test.ts lines 353 and 357 (ARM-7KQ4-XM2H-9). The plan lists log-privacy.test.ts as 'unchanged' (OB40, OB97 rows), and neither SC9 nor C21 lists these files. So either the new test fails on Phase 1 files, or its 'every product literal' claim is false. The brief also flags hard-coded ARM in tests.
findings.fix: List both files as stated replacements, with their canaries switched to the DEM or a synthetic prefix while each assertion keeps its meaning. Or state that the scan targets a defined literal pattern and explicitly exempts these canaries, with the reason.

findings.evidence: SC5 defines writeAudit's entry as 'a union of the actions listed in RD4 and ST', and C9 calls the list closed. But GN2 writes product.create { product_id } and GN3 writes batch.create { batch_id, product_id, kits }, and neither action is in RD4 or ST. audit-subject.test.ts checks 'every action' of that union. As written, the closed writer would refuse the generator's and the seed's audit rows, or the implementer would have to widen the list without the plan saying so. SC5 is also jade-o07's step, while the actions belong to later beads, and the plan does not say which bead adds each shape.
findings.fix: Name the full Phase 2 action list in one place: code.redeem, kit.attach, code.lockout, code.throttle, product.create and batch.create, plus ST's later actions. Give each its subject shape, and say which bead adds each shape to writeAudit and to audit-subject.test.ts.

findings.evidence: GN2 says that under APP_ENV=production both codes:product and the generator refuse unless 'the operator types the slug and label back'. Under staging and production 'they also require --confirm <slug>/<label>'. codes:product takes only --slug, --name and --prefix and has no label, so its production and staging confirmation is undefined. GN6's confirmation tests would have to guess.
findings.fix: Give codes:product its own confirmation, such as typing the slug and prefix back and --confirm <slug>. Have GN6 test it separately from the generator's <slug>/<label> form.
